data.one_liner: Low-level cross-platform audio recorder plugin using miniaudio with real-time waveform, FFT and volume.
data.what_it_does: A low-level audio recording plugin built with miniaudio that supports recording to WAV and Ogg Opus formats. It offers real-time volume, audio wave, and FFT data extraction, silence detection, and native hardware presets across multiple platforms.
use_when: You need low-level audio recording with cross-platform support including web WASM.
You require real-time audio visualization metrics like waveform and FFT data.
You need silence detection or specific hardware audio input presets.
avoid_when: You only need basic audio playback without recording functionality.
You want a high-level audio recording wrapper without handling low-level configuration.
strengths: Cross-platform support including Linux, Windows, Android, MacOS, iOS, and Web (WASM).
Real-time audio visualization events (waveform and FFT).
Built-in silence detection and customizable thresholds.
weaknesses: Requires manual permission handling for microphone access on mobile and desktop platforms.
Some advanced features like silence detection are restricted to specific PCM formats.
data.setup_notes: Requires microphone permissions in AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist, plus audio-input entitlements on macOS and optional GStreamer dependencies on Linux.

alternatives.name: record
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a more straightforward, high-level audio recording solution without low-level miniaudio bindings.

alternatives.name: audioplayers
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your primary focus is playing audio rather than low-level recording and visualization.
